title: The architect writes everything for the operator in plain words
situation: Asked to document the design, a fresh architect produced a dossier: concepts quoted word for word, every decision reprinted, and record numbers throughout, which mean nothing to the operator.
decision: Everything the architect writes for the operator, replies and documents alike, is in plain words for a layman, at the level of meaning: it explains in its own words rather than quoting the record, names a decision or concept by what it says and never by its number in the record, and leaves out history and mechanics unless asked.
consequences: The architect's definition says the same.
